## Findings
- claim-1: Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) with \(q=n-r\), graded by degree, and write \(\bar h_k\) for the image of \(h_k\). Since \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\) and \(\bar h_k=\bar s_{(k)}=0\) for \(k>q\), every element of \(A\) is a polynomial in \(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q\). Its positive-degree part has no constant monomial, hence lies in \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\). Conversely each \(\bar h_k\) has positive degree, so \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\subseteq A_+\). Therefore \[ A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q). \] (For \(q=0\), both sides are \(0\).)
- claim-2: For every ideal \(J_v\subseteq A\), \[ A_+J_v=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)J_v=\sum_{k=1}^{q}h_kJ_v. \] If \(J_v\) is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by its Schur classes \(s_\mu\), this subgroup is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by the Pieri products \[ h_k s_\mu,\qquad 1\le k\le q. \] By Pieri, \[ h_k s_\mu=\sum_{\substack{\nu\supseteq\mu\\ \nu/\mu\text{ a horizontal }k\text{-strip}}}s_\nu, \] with terms outside the \(q^r\)-box equal to \(0\) in \(A\).
## Strategy
Use the homogeneous grading of \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\). Since \(I_{r,q}\) is homogeneous and \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\), its quotient is generated by \(\bar h_k\). Box truncation gives \(\bar h_k=\bar s_{(k)}=0\) for \(k>q\). Thus \(A\) is generated by \(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q\), and its augmentation ideal is \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\), proving \(A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\).

For an ideal \(J_v\subseteq A\),
\[
A_+J_v=\sum_{k=1}^q\bar h_kJ_v.
\]
Assuming \(J_v\) is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by specified Schur classes \(s_\mu\), distributivity shows this subgroup is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by \(\bar h_ks_\mu\). Apply Pieri after projection to \(A\), deleting shapes outside \(q^r\).

## Gaps
The argument assumes the standard homogeneous box-truncation ideal \(I_{r,q}\) and the asserted Schur spanning description of \(J_v\). These hypotheses should be stated in the formal proof.
